title: Bounded-support torsion cohomology from closed-subscheme bounds
statement:
Let B be affine finite type over K and F a sheaf killed by a positive integer N. Assume F has zero geometric pullbacks at points of residue transcendence degree greater than a, and every closed affine subscheme of dimension at most a has torsion cohomological dimension at most a. Then H^q(B,F)=0 for q>a. Use torsion cohomological dimension as in [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd], the strict localization as in [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] when it occurs, and Krull dimension as in [def-kun-dimension]. The following verbatim Lean statement specifies all universes, hypotheses, scalar structures, sheaves and degrees:

theorem subsingleton_H_of_bounded_support
    {K : Type u} [Field K] {B : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine B]
    (b : B ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [LocallyOfFiniteType b] [QuasiCompact b] (a : ℕ)
    (hclosed : ∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Z] (i : Z ⟶ B) [IsClosedImmersion i],
      topologicalKrullDim Z ≤ (a : WithBot ℕ∞) →
        Z.HasTorsionCohomologicalDimensionLE a)
    (F : Sheaf B.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (N : ℕ)
    (hN : 0 < N) (hF : N • 𝟙 F = 0)
    (hstalk : ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsSepClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ B),
      (a : Cardinal.{u}) < residueFieldTrdeg b (s (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω)) →
        IsZero ((Etale.upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} s).obj F))
    (q : ℕ) (hq : a < q) : Subsingleton (Sheaf.H F q)

proof.text: Reuse the private proved Etale.dim_finite_union_le from SupportDimension via import all for finite unions of closed complements. The kernel of the restriction unit to an open U is killed by N and restricts to zero. Closed-support equivalence realizes it as direct image of a sheaf on the closed complement. The given closed-subscheme bound and the finite edge-map bijection kill cohomology above a.

Apply the existing proved finite closed-union dimension bound Etale.dim_finite_union_le from SupportDimension to the two closed complements. Their union is the complement of the intersection of the opens and has dimension at most a. The kernel factorization maps therefore make the supported subsheaves a directed family.
The existing locally-covering supportedIn theorem makes the family locally exhaustive. Cohomology commutes with its directed union; every class comes from one of the zero cohomology groups.
